clue.text: A chest fashioned to contain perfume

definitions.note: the answer is a small scented packet, standing here for the scent it holds

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made into a new form, so the letters of the two words are reworked

explanation.surface: A carpenter has built a chest to hold a bottle of scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' reworks the letters of A CHEST; 'to contain' is the link, telling us the answer is something that holds perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a little pouch of scented powder or herbs tucked among clothes to perfume them.

clue.text: Damage caused in shoe over a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the shoe comes on top of the time word

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog, a shoe
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Wear and tear on footwear over a long spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the word comes from workers throwing sabots, wooden shoes, into machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate wrecking of equipment or plans is destruction done on purpose.

clue.text: As a favour, turn up with help in speech

parts.note: to cock is to turn up, as a hat brim or an ear

indicators.note: in speech means as said aloud, so a spelling sounding the same is used

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: As a kindness, someone raises a hand to help in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'favour' here is an emblem such as a rosette, worn to show loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette worn on a hat is a badge of allegiance, like a ribbon given as a token.

clue.text: Using a diet, came out very thin

indicators.note: out means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone on a strict diet emerged looking gaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'came out', but signals that A DIET and CAME are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted and gaunt from hunger or illness, scrawny.

clue.text: Following orders, find nothing dishonest about the stamp

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: about means around, so the stamp word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: bent is slang for dishonest or corrupt
a die is a stamp for impressing coins or medals

explanation.surface: A dutiful employee finds no crookedness in how the official stamp is used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the stamp inside, splitting the dishonest word after its first letter; 'find' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries out instructions as told is compliant and dutiful.

clue.text: A gorgeous creature — Eve?

parts.note: a bird is slang for a woman, and Eve lived in the Garden of Eden, so she is a woman of Eden

explanation.surface: Was the first woman a stunning beauty?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a young woman; Eve lived in Eden, the earthly paradise, while the real creature is a brilliantly plumed New Guinea bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliantly plumed tropical species from New Guinea; Eve, a woman (bird) of Eden, fits the pun.

clue.text: Stunt man, in short

definitions.meaning: to stunt is to stop growing, to make appear small
a person of very small stature, a short man

explanation.surface: A stuntman described briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunt man' reads as one job; split it, a verb meaning to make look small, then a short man.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow by size is to make look small; a person of very restricted height is the noun sense.

clue.text: An excuse so naive is deplorable

indicators.note: deplorable means awful, a mess, so the letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A judgment that an excuse so naive is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deplorable' sounds like a verdict on the excuse, but it reshuffles SO NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge or a way of avoiding the question is a pretext.

clue.text: Not quite the top — there were seven against it

indicators.note: not quite means one short of the whole, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the best means the top, the finest

explanation.surface: Second best, with seven people ranged against it.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven Against Thebes is a Greek tragedy by Aeschylus about seven champions attacking the Greek city. 'Not quite' drops the last T of THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven champions besieged the ancient Greek city in the myth Aeschylus dramatised.

clue.text: Court officer troubles tart manageress

indicators.note: troubles means disturbs or upsets, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A court official is bothering a rude manageress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' scrambles TART and MANAGERESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An official in a court or legislature who keeps order is a ceremonial enforcer of discipline.

clue.text: Pirate to a listener, deer to a listener

indicators.note: to a listener means as it would strike someone hearing it said

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, and a listener is an ear, giving buck, an ear

explanation.surface: A riddle comparing how a pirate and a deer would sound to someone listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase does two jobs in turn: the first 'to a listener' signals a sound-alike, the second turns 'deer to a listener' into BUCK AN EAR, which said quickly matches the pirate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a sea robber of the Caribbean in the 1600s.

clue.text: Bestir oneself for a vigil

definitions.meaning: to rouse or stir from sleep, as a verb
read as two words, a wake: a watch kept over a dead body

explanation.surface: Get up and stay alert for a night of watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse from sleep is to come to wakefulness; a wake is a watch kept over the dead, so 'a' plus that word gives the second sense.

clue.text: Determining the whereabouts of a copy

definitions.meaning: finding where someone or something is, as a police search does
a drawing made by following lines through thin paper

explanation.surface: Locating where a copied document has ended up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking someone down is locating them; a duplicate drawn over an original through thin paper is the second sense.

clue.text: Foul play here at Wembley rather than at Lord's

definitions.text: Foul play here at Wembley rather than at Lord's

parts.words: Foul play here at Wembley rather than at Lord's
parts.note: Wembley is the English football stadium, Lord's the London cricket ground: in football this is an infringement, in cricket the same words name half the field

explanation.surface: A remark that something counts as cheating in football but not in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is England's national football stadium; Lord's is London's famous cricket ground. In football the word is an infringement by an attacker; in cricket 'off side' is simply the half of the field facing the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A football player ahead of the ball and the last defender commits this infringement, while cricket uses the same words for one half of the pitch.

clue.text: Some expectations were

parts.note: a sly nod to the title of a Dickens novel about Pip, read as a statement that certain hopes were large

explanation.surface: A rueful admission that some hopes were once high.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue completes the Dickens novel title 'Great Expectations' while seeming to say that some hopes existed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel of Pip's hopes is titled with this adjective meaning large or grand before 'Expectations'.

clue.text: Sire, bo'h ways it's obvious

indicators.note: both ways means the father word is read in two directions, backwards here before it appears forwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for a father, a sire
a sire is a father, a parent

explanation.surface: A courtier tells the king that something is plain whichever way you look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' tells you to use 'Sire' twice: first the short word for father read backwards, then the longer word for a father read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apparent is plain to see, clearly evident.

clue.text: Make an anagram of back scope

parts.note: rear means the back
range means scope, extent

explanation.surface: An instruction to jumble the letters of 'back scope'.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like an anagram instruction for BACK SCOPE, but nothing is jumbled: the definition is 'Make an anagram of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forming an anagram means putting the letters into a new order.

clue.text: Equine disease is amazing

definitions.meaning: a disorder of horses causing them to lurch and stumble
astonishes, bowls over, as a verb in the third person

explanation.surface: A horse's illness is remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease makes horses reel; something that astounds you is the verb sense.

clue.text: Give him his due and he'll stop being one

definitions.text: Give him his due and he'll stop being one

parts.words: Give him his due and he'll stop being one
parts.note: read literally, once a person owed money is paid what is due, he is no longer owed anything

explanation.surface: Grudging praise: credit someone fairly and he will stop complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give him his due' sounds like an idiom for fair acknowledgement, but here it means paying a debt to the person it is owed to.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender is owed money; once repaid in full, that person is owed nothing more.

clue.text: One who has no illusions about a heel

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to heel is to lean over, as a ship does, to list

explanation.surface: Someone sees a scoundrel clearly for what he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a scoundrel, but it is the sailing sense: a ship heels or lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist who sees things as they truly are is clear-eyed.

clue.text: Something of value a girl returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A girl brings back a treasured possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the girl's name, as in Hardy's heroine, from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession or quality worth having is a valuable resource, as on a balance sheet.

clue.text: Fly, Clotho!

definitions.meaning: an angler's lure that revolves in the water
Clotho is the Fate who spins the thread of life

explanation.surface: A command to flee, addressed to one of the Fates.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Clotho is the Fate who spins the thread of life. 'Fly' looks like the verb, but is a fishing lure.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving bait used by anglers is one sense; the Fate who works the thread is one who spins.

clue.text: Copper has the last word about penetration

indicators.note: about means around, so the last word goes round the metal

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman insists on having the final say about penetrating an area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen insight, sharpness of mind, is mental penetration.

clue.text: Fellow hired a wreath

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a fellow, a man
let means rented out, hired

explanation.surface: A man has rented a floral wreath for an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or circlet of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: Dead right afterwards

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone dead right about what happened afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' reads as one phrase meaning entirely right; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsequently, at a following time.

clue.text: Beloved oarswoman

definitions.meaning: a dear one, as an adjective, much loved
Grace ..., the lighthouse keeper's daughter who rowed out to rescue shipwrecked sailors in 1838

explanation.surface: A tribute to a much-loved woman who rows.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling was a Northumberland lighthouse keeper's daughter, a British heroine for rowing out to a wreck in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherished person is dear; the famous English rescuer who rowed a coble to save sailors bore this surname.

clue.text: Chinese communist not a wet

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter given by a is left out

parts.note: a Maoist follows Mao Zedong's Chinese communism

explanation.surface: A Chinese communist insists he is no feeble moderate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from MAOIST. 'wet' looks like the British political insult for a feeble moderate, but it is the plain adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp, slightly wet, is the sense: humid or dewy.

clue.text: Quixotic companion involved in treason

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A loyal companion of Don Quixote is caught up in a treason plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' looks like a link telling us the companion took part, but it scrambles IN and TREASON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's bony old horse in Cervantes's novel is the companion of his travels.

clue.text: He's barely visible

parts.note: barely means only just, but reread as in bare, the person is seen without clothes

explanation.surface: Someone can only just be seen in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' wants to mean 'hardly'; read it as 'in the bare' and the man is seen naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes about unclothed, visible in the bare.

clue.text: Ruins young lady, the backsliding knight

parts.note: deb is short for debutante, a young society lady

indicators.note: backsliding means going backwards, so the knight's title is turned round

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A society girl's reputation is ruined by a knight who lapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the backsliding' reads the knight's title from right to left. 'Ruins' looks like a verb but is the noun, the remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubble and scattered remains after destruction are wreckage.
